title: Bijectivity of the induced completion map
statement: Under the same Noetherian local hypotheses, maximal-ideal equality and residue-field bijectivity, any flat ring homomorphism between the adic completions compatible with the original local map is bijective.

proof.text: The completions are local, with maximal ideals extended from A and B and residue fields A/mA and B/mB. Compatibility and hmax give mR S = nS, hence continuity; approximation by elements of A and separation of S identify the given map with the canonical componentwise map.
The special fibre B/mA B is A/mA by hmax and hres. Apply finiteness after completion. The levelwise formula and separation identify its map with the supplied map, so S is finite over R.

Use assumed flatness and finite flat local freeness. Reduction modulo mR has dimension one, so the finite basis has one member e. Write 1 = u e; u is outside the maximal ideal because otherwise 1 lies in nS. Thus u is a unit and 1 is a basis, proving bijectivity.

theorem completion_map_bijective
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B]
    (φ : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom φ]
    (hmax : Ideal.map φ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B)
    (hres : Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) φ
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal_comap φ).ge))
    (φhat : AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A →+*
      AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) B)
    (hcomp : φhat.comp (algebraMap A
      (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A)) =
      (algebraMap B (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) B)).comp φ)
    (hflat : φhat.Flat) : Function.Bijective φhat
